evidence.reason: Proposal workload entrypoint: appends Entry{Index,Term,Data} to node.log and emits AppendEntries via appendMessagesLocked; returns ErrNotLeader when not leader.
Normal protocol input boundary for request_vote/append_entries messages; validates To, clones, processes under mutex.
Membership changes are explicitly omitted, so no membership_change entrypoint exists to discover.

external_input.boundary: Analyze the Mini Raft protocol core in this repository. Real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary.
external_input.reason: The protocol core exposes a synchronous proposal entrypoint Node.Propose (leader-gated) and a message input boundary Node.Step. No new business-input API is needed; discovery alone satisfies v0.1.
limitations: membership_change external input is absent by design (doc.go:5).
Propose commits the entry immediately in the leader (node.go:164) — simplified commit semantics with no separate apply stage.

evidence.reason: Node creation entrypoint with config validation; sets running=true, role=follower, random seed.
Sets running=false; Tick/Step/Propose return ErrPaused while paused (see node_test.go TestPauseIsNotCrashRecovery).
Sets running=true; all state retained, no crash/restart semantics.
Comment: Node owns both persistent-looking and volatile-looking state in one object; Pause/Resume do not define crash recovery — no invented state split needed.

lifecycle_control.boundary: Analyze the Mini Raft protocol core in this repository. Real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary.
lifecycle_control.reason: Creation (NewNode), stop/start (Pause/Resume) and state ownership are already exposed and testable; the code explicitly documents that Pause/Resume are scheduler pause, not crash recovery, and that all state lives in one object — so no persistent/volatile split decision is required.
limitations: No crash recovery API exists; durable storage is outside the system boundary (doc.go:5).
Persistent/volatile state split is intentionally not modeled (node.go:46-47); tests must not assume one.

evidence.reason: Documented: Send immediately calls the target node's Step method, so delivery is synchronous and uncontrollable — capture/suppression must be inserted before it.
Single outbound choke point: iterates all produced messages and calls transport.Send; all campaign/append/response paths return []Message into emit.
transport.Send(message) is the last controllable point before the environment-owned send path.
Transport is an injected interface (Config.Transport, node.go:31/79), so a wrapper can intercept Send without touching protocol logic.
Deep-copies entries/payloads; a captured message can be retained as a stable snapshot after Send returns.
Heartbeats are appendMessagesLocked(nil) on the same emit path — no separate bypass channel.
Acceptance tests reference raft.NewControlledTransport/MessageMeta/ListPending/Inject, which do not exist in the source (find_symbol returns no declaration) — the missing additive seam.

message_capture.boundary: Analyze the Mini Raft protocol core in this repository. Real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary.
message_capture.gap: No ControlledTransport, MessageMeta, pending store, or capture/suppress logic exists; MC1/MC2 acceptance tests cannot compile or pass under the consensusseam tag.
message_capture.reason: No capture seam exists today: MemoryTransport.Send synchronously calls target.Step, so outbound messages always enter the uncontrollable send path. However, every outbound message (vote requests, vote responses, append entries, append responses, heartbeats-as-empty-append) funnels through the single choke point Node.emit -> Transport.Send, and Transport is injected via Config — a clean additive wrapper (ControlledTransport + MessageMeta + ListPending) can capture and suppress before the wrapped transport, with no Node changes. Message.Clone already provides stable snapshots.
limitations: MemoryTransport.Delivered() records post-delivery copies only (transport.go:38), not pre-send capture.
No retries, snapshots, or forwarded requests exist, so there are no capture bypasses beyond the single Send path.
Real networking and durable storage are outside the boundary; capture applies only to the in-process Transport seam.
message_capture.suggested_direction: Add package-level ControlledTransport wrapping Transport: Send() stores message.Clone() with a stable ID and monotonic CaptureSequence and does not forward; expose ListPending() []MessageMeta. No changes to Node or emit required.

evidence.reason: Normal protocol input boundary: rejects wrong target (ErrWrongTarget), clones message, processes synchronously, returns errors such as ErrPaused.
Target selection by nodes[stable.To] and ErrUnknownNode on missing target — the delivery mechanism an Inject can reuse.
stepLocked(message.Clone()) — injected messages are processed through the identical path as normal deliveries.
MC3 requires Inject(id) to consume exactly one pending message, deliver to its recorded target, and keep it pending on failure (lines 116-134) — API does not exist yet.

message_injection.boundary: Analyze the Mini Raft protocol core in this repository. Real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary.
message_injection.gap: No pending store or Inject(id) exists; consume-on-success / keep-on-failure semantics must be added at the transport layer.
message_injection.reason: Node.Step is a clean synchronous normal input boundary (validates message.To == node.id, clones, processes under mutex) and MemoryTransport already selects targets by message.To from its node registry. The missing piece is additive transport-layer logic: Inject(id) removes the selected pending message only after successful delivery through the wrapped transport (target.Step), leaving it pending on error — exactly matching MC3.
limitations: Injection failure modes (ErrUnknownNode, ErrPaused, wrapped transport errors) must leave the pending message untouched.
No deduplication or replay protection exists beyond per-pending-ID consumption; re-capture of equivalent messages is possible.
Injection is only meaningful for in-process nodes registered with the underlying MemoryTransport; real networking is outside the boundary.
message_injection.suggested_direction: Implement ControlledTransport.Inject(id): look up the pending MessageMeta, deliver the stored message via the wrapped transport's Send (which reaches the target's Step), and remove from pending only on nil error; return the transport error otherwise. Additive, no Node changes.

evidence.reason: Exposes ID, Running, Role, Term, Vote, Leader, CommitIndex, LastIndex, RandomizedElectionTimeout under lock.
LastIndex = len(node.log) provides log-range observation.
Returns deep copies of all delivered messages — the only global observation channel.

observation.boundary: Analyze the Mini Raft protocol core in this repository. Real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary.
observation.reason: Node.Status exposes role, term, vote, leader, commit index, last index, randomized election timeout, and running; MemoryTransport.Delivered exposes delivered-message history. This is the minimum per-node/global state needed by the MC capability checks (they verify Status().Term and Status().LastIndex).
limitations: No applied_index: the core has no apply loop (leader sets commit directly at proposal), so no applied index exists to expose.
No log-content accessor: Status exposes LastIndex but not entries.
No global multi-node aggregate; tests must assemble per-node Status and Delivered().

evidence.reason: node.random = rand.New(rand.NewSource(time.Now().UnixNano() + int64(config.ID))) — wall-clock seed, no injection seam.
randomizedElectionTimeout = electionTick + node.random.Intn(electionTick) — the single protocol-randomness consumer.

randomness_control.boundary: Analyze the Mini Raft protocol core in this repository. Real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary.
randomness_control.gap: No seed/rand-source injection point exists; identical initial state does not currently produce repeatable election timeouts.
randomness_control.reason: Protocol randomness (randomized election timeout) is used at exactly one call site, but the rand source is constructed internally from time.Now().UnixNano()+ID with no injection point, so runs are not repeatable. A localized additive patch (optional seed or rand source in Config) makes it deterministic without restructuring.
limitations: Randomness is used only for election timeout randomization; no other random choices exist in the core.
README (lines 48-49) notes the transform pipeline does not yet patch randomness, so determinism requires the future patch.
randomness_control.suggested_direction: Add optional RandomSeed int64 or RandomSource *rand.Rand to Config; default to the current time-based behavior when unset, and use it in NewNode.

evidence.reason: Advances exactly one unit of protocol logical time; increments heartbeat/election elapsed counters and emits messages.
Election triggers only when electionElapsed >= randomizedElectionTimeout — no direct timeout-forcing operation.
Heartbeats fire when heartbeatElapsed >= heartbeatTick, purely tick-driven.
time.Now() is used only to seed randomness; it never advances protocol-observed time.

time_control.boundary: Analyze the Mini Raft protocol core in this repository. Real networking, durable storage, and application process behavior are outside the boundary.
time_control.reason: Protocol time is advanced exclusively by the explicit Node.Tick logical-time API; there are no wall-clock timers, goroutines, or sleeps in the core, and no ForceTimeout/ForceElection operation exists (campaigning occurs only when electionElapsed reaches the randomized timeout). time.Now() appears only as a randomness seed, not as protocol-observed time.
limitations: Tick is per-node; a multi-node test must call Tick on each node to advance the whole cluster.
Wall clock is used indirectly for the randomness seed (node.go:80) — affects election-timeout values, not the tick timeline.
No injectable Clock variant exists, but explicit_tick alone satisfies the accepted v0.1 forms.
